title: Circuits - 123 school
heading: Circuits
intro: All the data you need is in the question. Round to the correct number of digits.

questions.question: How is an ammeter placed in a circuit?
How is a voltmeter placed in a circuit?
What is Ohm's law?
A current of 0.50 A flows through a resistor of 12 Ω. What is the voltage?
The voltage across a resistor is 9.0 V and the current is 0.30 A. What is the resistance?
A 46 Ω heating element is connected to 230 V. What is the current?
What is the unit of resistance?
What is true for the current in a series circuit?

answers.a: The current is zero at every component
answers.b: The current divides between the components
answers.c: The current is greatest at the first lamp
answers.d: The current is the same everywhere

questions.question: What is true for the voltage in a series circuit?

answers.a: The voltage is greatest at the last component
answers.c: The source voltage is shared between the components
answers.d: Every component has the full source voltage

questions.question: What is true for the voltage across components connected in parallel?

answers.a: The voltage is zero at every component
answers.b: The voltage is shared between the components
answers.d: The voltage across each component is the same

questions.question: What is true for the current in a parallel circuit?

answers.a: The total current is the sum of the currents through the branches
answers.b: The current in each branch is equal to the total current
answers.c: The current through the branches is always equal
answers.d: The current disappears in the first branch

questions.question: What happens to the other lamps if one lamp burns out in a series circuit?

answers.b: The other lamps burn more brightly
answers.d: Only the lamp next to it goes out

questions.question: What happens to the other lamps if one lamp burns out in a parallel circuit?

answers.a: The other lamps go out after a few seconds
answers.b: Only the first lamp stays on

questions.question: How are the appliances in a house connected?

answers.a: Only in series with the meter

questions.question: Two resistors of 10 Ω and 15 Ω are in series. What is the equivalent resistance?
Three resistors of 8.0 Ω are in series. What is the equivalent resistance?
Two resistors of 6.0 Ω and 3.0 Ω are in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance? (1/R<sub>v</sub> = 1/R<sub>1</sub> + 1/R<sub>2</sub>)
Two equal resistors of 20 Ω are in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance?
What happens to the equivalent resistance if you connect an extra resistor in parallel?

answers.d: The equivalent resistance stays the same

questions.question: Two resistors of 10 Ω and 15 Ω are in series on a 12 V source. What is the current?
The same circuit: 10 Ω and 15 Ω in series on 12 V, current 0.48 A. What is the voltage across the 10 Ω resistor?
A 6.0 Ω resistor and a 12 Ω resistor are in parallel on 12 V. What is the total current?
In a parallel circuit, two ammeters in the branches read 0.30 A and 0.20 A. What is the total current?
In a series circuit, two voltmeters across two lamps read 4.0 V and 2.0 V. What is the source voltage?
You connect two 1.5 V batteries in series. What is the total voltage?
A 6.0 V lamp has a power of 3.0 W. What is the current through the lamp? (P = U × I)
How does the resistance of a thin wire compare with that of a thick wire (same material and length)?

answers.b: The thin wire has a smaller resistance
answers.c: The thin wire has no resistance
answers.d: The thin wire has a greater resistance

questions.question: What happens to the resistance of a wire if you make the wire twice as long?

answers.a: The resistance becomes four times as small
answers.c: The resistance becomes twice as large
answers.d: The resistance becomes two times as small

questions.question: What does an NTC do at a higher temperature?
What does an LDR do when more light falls on it?
What do you use a variable resistor for?

answers.a: To control the resistance, and with it the current

questions.question: What happens in a short circuit?

answers.c: A very large current flows because the resistance is very small
